author: RyanJohnson1998
quote:
TL/DR: 
The Verdict: 1/10
Grand Theft Auto VI is a monument to modern AAA hubris. It asks you to wait thirteen years, pay top dollar for an empty box with no disc, suffer through 30fps performance and game breaking bugs, and grind through artificial wait timers in a watered-down story. Rockstar didn't deliver a revolution they delivered a gilded storefront disguised as a video game. 

The Review:
Thirteen years. 
Over a decade of trailers, delays, corporate excuses, and a reported two-billion-dollar budget: all culminating in what might be the most cynical, anti-consumer, and technically broken release in modern gaming history. 

If you were hoping Grand Theft Auto VI would be the triumphant return of the unapologetic, boundary-pushing Rockstar Games of old, prepare for a massive, overpriced reality check. 
Here is a breakdown of how Rockstar managed to fumble the most anticipated game on the planet. A thirteen-year wait for a Cyberpunk Style mess you would assume that taking more than a decade to develop a single video game. while milking GTA Online for billions in the meantime would guarantee a spotless, airtight launch.

Instead, players were greeted on day one by a buggy, unoptimized wreck that immediately drew comparisons to Cyberpunk 2077. Across both PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, the game is riddled with immersion **** glitches: Game-Breaking softlocks: Repeated crashes during the opening prologue, hard freezes, and an early Lucia mission softlock right outside a bank that completely halts story progression.

Broken Physics and Geometry: Launch-day footage is flooded with aircraft clipping straight through ****, characters falling endlessly beneath the map, NPCs swimming sideways through concrete, and vehicles spontaneously detonating or launching into the stratosphere from minor fender-benders.   Performance Compromises: Despite the endless wait, console players were slapped with a 30fps cap, accompanied by frame drops, missing textures, and cut-out audio. 
The Ultimate Anti-Consumer Cash Grab: No Disc, No Ownership Even worse than the technical state of the game is the sheer corporate greed surrounding how it is sold. For a franchise built on iconic physical releases complete with fold-out paper maps and thick manuals Rockstar and Take-Two decided to spit in the face of collectors and everyday consumers by shipping GTA VI without a physical disc.
If you walked into a retail store, you weren't buying a game; you were paying full AAA price for a hollow plastic case containing a glorified piece of paper with a download code and not even a physical map to soften the blow. 
By killing the physical disc, Rockstar effectively: Eliminated True Ownership: You don't own GTA VI; you are renting a revocable digital license. 
Destroyed Resale and Lending: You cannot lend the game to a friend, trade it in at a local shop, or buy a used copy. Every single person who wants to play is forced to pay full price directly into Take-Two’s digital storefront. 
Trapped Pre-Order Buyers: By locking down pre-loads early and stripping away standard retail alternatives, consumers were cornered into digital lock-in before the public ever saw the 30fps cap or the launch-day bugs.
Trading Classic GTA Chaos for Tedious "Realism" and Gated Grinds. Perhaps the most disappointing part of GTA VI is that it actively abandons the fast-paced, satirical DNA that made Vice City, San Andreas, and even GTA V fun to play. Instead of leaning into classic arcade chaos, Rockstar doubled down on the sluggish, hyper-realistic mechanics of Red Dead Redemption 2 and then padded the campaign with artificial roadblocks. 
Artificial Story Gating: Rather than letting you play through the narrative at your own pace, the campaign introduces mandatory wait timers and cash hurdles between story missions. Want to see what happens next? Go grind petty store robberies or fence cars until the game decides you're allowed to progress.   Nickel and Diming Basic Convenience: Even basic quality-of-life features from older titles have been turned into tedious money sinks- you can't even skip a cab ride without paying an extra $100 fee on top of the fare.
Safe, Toothless Writing: Gone is the sharp, irreverent bite that once defined the series. Critics and longtime fans (Myself included) alike have pointed out that the dialogue and narrative payoffs feel sanitized, flat, and noticeably weaker than past entries clearly designed to funnel players away from a forgettable single-player campaign and straight into the next decade of GTA Online microtransactions. 
The Verdict: 2/10
Grand Theft Auto VI is a monument to modern AAA hubris. It asks you to wait thirteen years, pay top dollar for an empty box with no disc, suffer through 30fps performance and game-breaking bugs, and grind through artificial wait timers in a watered-down story. Rockstar didn't deliver a revolution, they delivered a gilded storefront disguised as a video game. 

SHAME.
